idiom_name: case class with default parameters + named arguments + copy()
implementation_notes: A case class with default parameter values is the valid base instance, named arguments let a test supply only the fields it names, and the compiler-generated copy(email = "bad@example.com") is the override step - the builder object never exists. Put factories in the companion object (def aUser: User = User()), keep the case class immutable so copy is the only way to vary it, and place validation in the companion or in require() so production and test construction take the same path. Hand-written builders remain the answer only for conditional or staged construction (parsers, DSLs); for deep graphs, compose factories rather than growing one builder.
code_sketch:
case class User(
  name: String = "Ada Lovelace",
  email: String = "ada@example.com",
  age: Int = 30,
)

val u = User().copy(email = "bad@example.com")   // only the asserted field
assert(!canSendInvoice(u))
pitfalls: copy is shallow: nested case classes and collections are shared, so a test mutating a nested collection changes the default for later tests.
Positional construction still compiles (User("bad@example.com") assigns the email to name), so the pattern's safety depends on consistently naming arguments.
Defaults in the case-class header are visible to production code; a test-flavoured default (fake ids, clocks) inside the domain type leaks into the application.
